subject: STRING statement
notes: kb/Work PB664 (wave 44). SR1 is TWO sentences over FIVE operand positions and it was enforced at ONE of them. (a) 'all identifiers, except identifier-4, shall be described implicitly or explicitly as usage display or national' screened identifier-3 only, so `STRING P DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO A` over a USAGE POINTER sender compiled clean and stored 'WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime.CellPointer' - the CLR carrier's type name - through OperandText's `_ => Read(p).ToString()` arm, and a COMP, PACKED or INDEX sender or DELIMITED BY operand did the same. (b) 'All literals shall be described as alphanumeric, boolean, or national literals' was enforced nowhere: `STRING 12 ...` and `... DELIMITED BY 5` were accepted. (c) the second sentence - 'If any one of literal-1, literal-2, identifier-1, identifier-2, or identifier-3 is of class national, then all shall be of class national' - was enforced nowhere: a PIC N sender into a PIC X receiver transcoded silently. All three are now ONE predicate asked at EVERY position the rule names (Sr1Offence / Sr1MixesNational, reported through the one Sr1Reject site, COBOL1626), the class read from the ONE 8.5.2.1 Table-2 reader IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf, and OperandText's fall-through is now a loud invariant failure instead of text. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE WITNESSED, which is what a rejection rule needs: the negatives pin the refusals (usage, numeric literal, pointer, national mix) and conformance:cases/14.9.43-STRING/pb664_string_operand_screen pins five ADMITTED spellings so the screen cannot over-reach - including identifier-4 as a USAGE BINARY item, which witnesses the rule's own exemption rather than assuming it, plus a usage-display NUMERIC sender (SR1 admits it; SR8 constrains it), a GROUP sender and a numeric-edited sender. ENFORCING IT CAUGHT A GOLDEN ASSERTING A RULE OVER ILLEGAL SOURCE: conformance:cases/14.6.13.1.3-Fatal-exception-conditions/ec_data_not_finite carried `STRING WS-INF DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO WS-TXT` over a COMP-2 item, which SR1 refuses and SR8 refuses again; that leg is removed and the file now says why (the MOVE-to-alphanumeric twin is refused by 14.9.25.3 SR10 / Table 16, so neither chokepoint is reachable from conforming source with a float). ONE ADMITTED SHAPE HAS NO POSITIVE WITNESS AND IT IS NOT THIS RULE'S DOING: an ALL-NATIONAL STRING, which SR1 admits, dies at run time in a NotImplementedCobolFeature stage whose message mis-cites this rule ('STRING INTO receiver ... usage display required, ISO 14.9.43.3 SR1'). That is the STRING emitter's staged national transfer - 14.9.43.4 GR3 a)'s 'national-to-national moves' arm - charged there, not here, and registered as a lead in the wave-44 report.
